The skin-cancer target identity is a melanoma/non-melanoma umbrella; the evidence base is nevus-count melanoma risk quantification, so any non-melanoma (keratinocyte-carcinoma) component of the target is not covered by the cited evidence and is recorded as a guard.
governanceNotes: D1 batch 27 (2026-09-23): one bounded skin-cancer-risk association authored from nevus-count melanoma epidemiology; the pooled atypical-nevi relative risk is melanoma-specific, and the umbrella target identity's non-melanoma share is an explicit evidence-scope guard recorded on the edge.

The risk-factor relationship is a marker-of-risk proposition (nevi as clinical indicators of constitutive and UV-interaction melanoma risk), not a progressive disease pathway; no somatic transformation-of-individual-nevi claim is asserted at the mapping level.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: The pooled 46-study meta-analysis found a substantially increased melanoma relative risk with increasing nevus burden (atypical nevi 5 versus 0: RR 6.36, 95% CI 3.80-10.33; 101-120 common nevi versus <15: RR 6.89, 95% CI 4.63-10.25; Gandini 2005), and the Brisbane Naevus Morphology Study quantified the joint effect of high nevus count with MC1R red-hair genotype on melanoma odds (MC1R R/R with >=20 naevi: OR 25.1, 95% CI 8.4-82.7 versus wild-type with 0-4 naevi; absolute risk to age 75 of 23.3% in the highest-risk group; Duffy 2019).
nexusClaim.causationStatus: The meta-analytic and cohort risk estimates are population-level associations from a risk-marker phenotype, not established causation for an individual lesion: nevus count is a composite marker of melanocytic propensity and sun-exposure history, and the individual pathway from a given dysplastic nevus to a diagnosed melanoma (versus de novo melanoma or an intervening unrelated lesion) cannot be established from these designs; the identity's clinical meaning as a surveillance designation is retained.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: A hypothesized nevus-burden melanoma-risk pathway: an increased number of melanocytic nevi, including cytologically atypical nevi, reflects an expanded population of melanocytes that have acquired or are predisposed to acquire oncogenic changes, so a larger nevus burden raises the statistical probability that melanoma arises in association with the nevus field; the Duffy 2019 genotype analysis shows this risk is multiplicative with inherited MC1R red-hair alleles and high ultraviolet exposure, meaning the nevus phenotype operates as one component of a multifactorial risk state rather than an autonomous causal agent.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: The cited evidence quantifies population melanoma risk by nevus count and genotype, not individual lesion-to-tumor causation; whether any diagnosed melanoma arose from a documented dysplastic nevus versus de novo, whether the nevus phenotype is the operative marker in the individual, and how the umbrella target's non-melanoma share relates to the melanoma-specific evidence all require case-specific dermatologic review; no probability estimate is asserted.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Documented dysplastic-nevus-syndrome phenotype (multiple clinically atypical nevi, histologic confirmation where performed); pathology-confirmed melanoma diagnosis with anatomic and chronologic relationship to the nevus field; dermoscopic or histologic linkage of the melanoma to a specific nevus where claimed; UV-exposure and phenotypic risk-factor documentation; dermatology review of the individual relationship
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: De novo melanoma unassociated with any pre-existing nevus
Melanoma driven by UV-exposure history independent of nevus phenotype
Keratinocyte (basal- or squamous-cell) carcinoma outside the melanoma evidence scope
CDKN2A-family melanoma syndrome or other inherited predisposition as the operative driver
Metastatic or misclassified pigmented lesion not arising in the nevus field

evidenceGaps: Documented dysplastic-nevus-syndrome phenotype (multiple clinically atypical nevi, histologic confirmation where performed); pathology-confirmed melanoma diagnosis with anatomic and chronologic relationship to the nevus field; dermoscopic or histologic linkage of the melanoma to a specific nevus where claimed; UV-exposure and phenotypic risk-factor documentation; dermatology review of the individual relationship
suggestions.rationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY: the nevus-count melanoma risk gradient is one of the strongest risk-marker associations in dermatology, but it is a population risk-factor relationship and a surveillance proposition, not an established individual causal pathway; no causation or probability is asserted.

sourceReferences.citation: Gandini S, Sera F, Cattaruzza MS, et al. Meta-analysis of risk factors for cutaneous melanoma: I. Common and atypical naevi. Eur J Cancer. 2005 Jan;41(1):28-44. PMID 15617989.
sourceReferences.note: Pooled random-effects meta-analysis of 46 observational studies: atypical nevi 5 versus 0 carried melanoma RR 6.36 (95% CI 3.80-10.33) and 101-120 common naevi versus <15 carried RR 6.89 (95% CI 4.63-10.25); the dose-response anchor for the nevus-count-to-melanoma-risk association.
